parts.title: Listening Passage 1
parts.transcriptHtml:
Sally: Morning. Thanks for coming round. I’m Sally.

Builder: Morning. So just before we get started, I’ll just make a few notes. So, we’re at 15 Hill Street?

Sally: Yes, that’s right.

Builder: Okay, great. And then I need to write down your contact information, just for the office, you know. So first, what’s your surname please, Sally?

Sally: It’s Keyworth. I’ll spell that. K e y w o r t h.

Builder: And your phone number? I’ve got that somewhere. Yes. 0275846613?

Sally: That’s right.

Builder: Okay, Sally. So what building work would you like to have done?

Sally: Well, let’s go into the kitchen first. So you see it’s quite dark in here. We’ve tried having a few lights fitted, but it hasn’t really made any difference. So what we’ve decided is the window is too small. We’d like a larger one.

Builder: That shouldn’t be a problem. And is there anything else you’d like done in the kitchen?

Sally: Well, at this time of year, I mean, I shouldn’t complain really, but I wish it wasn’t so hot in here. Is there anything you can do about that? Air conditioning?

Builder: It’s too expensive. How about a fan then?

Sally: Yes. That would be perfect.

Builder: Righto. And what’s next, Sally?

Sally: Well, if we walk through into the bathroom, The thing is, when my father’s staying, he can’t use the bath. So I thought here on the back wall, I’d like you to fit a shower. Is that possible?

Builder: Shouldn’t be too hard. I’ll get you some brochures because there are a few ways of doing that.

Sally: Thanks. Now those tiles on the wall look new, so do you want to keep those?

Sally: Yes. The tiles are new, but actually my husband doesn’t like them. We want to change to those very small ones. But do I have to choose a color now?

Builder: You can do that later. I’ll get some charts for you to look at.

Sally: Now the last thing, let’s walk outside. I need to show you some things outside the house.

Builder: Righto. Oh, nice garden. And the fence looks in good condition.

Sally: Yes. It’s new, but the thing is the gate. It’s too low. You have to bend down to open it. We need something that’s higher.

Builder: Right. I’ll see to that.

Sally: Then the other thing is the garage here. We had a break in, actually.

Builder: Yeah. I can see. The door should be fine, but the lock, I’ll replace that, shall I?

Sally: Yes. Thanks.

Sally: Then also, if you step back here and look up on the roof, you can see that it’s damaged.

Builder: Did that happen in the storm a couple of weeks ago?

Sally: Yes, that’s right.

Builder: I’ll get up there and take a look at that then. That might be quite a big job, but I’ll get back to you once I’ve had a look.

Sally: Okay.

Builder: I can see that your rain gutter is broken as well.

Sally: Can you fix that?

Builder: Well, I’ll need to replace it, maybe with a steel one. It’d be stronger.

Sally: No. Plastic will be fine, thanks. It’s cheaper.

Builder: Okay.

Sally: And that’s everything, I think. Is there any other information you need? What about a start date?

Builder: Well, I’m completely booked all April, and I’ve got a job on May 5. That’ll be a few days, so let’s say May 8..

Sally: Okay.

Builder: Now what about a key in case you’re out? We have a security code. I’ll give you that. It’s a mix of letters and numbers. The code is AG4176.

Builder: Got that. Okay. We’ll organize some.
